::: {.tut-standfirst}
Common questions for people getting started with Saíra to prepare and publish biodiversity data in Darwin Core.
:::

## Installation and requirements

### Do I need to know how to program to use Saíra?

::: {.faq-card}
No. The app for Windows and Linux opens like any other program, and all the work happens through menus, buttons and tables. The R package, for macOS or for people who prefer R, needs one line of code to open the app.
:::

### What do I need to have installed?

::: {.faq-card}
For the app on Windows or Linux, nothing: it has its own R. The R package needs **R** 4.1 or later. RStudio is optional. See the requirements in [Installation and first steps](tutorials/01-installation.qmd).
:::

### How do I install Saíra?

::: {.faq-card}
Download the app from the [releases page](https://github.com/rogerio-onza/saira/releases/latest) or install the R package. [Installation and first steps](tutorials/01-installation.qmd) shows both paths.
:::

### The R package install is taking a long time. Is that normal?

::: {.faq-card}
Yes. The first install of the R package downloads and compiles the dependencies and can take a few minutes. The app already has them.
:::

### I updated Saíra, but it still looks like the old version. What happened?

::: {.faq-card}
**In the R package**, R was almost always not restarted: the open session keeps the old version in memory. Close and reopen R (in RStudio, *Session › Restart R*) and open the app again. Saíra detects this and shows a warning. **In the app**, `pak::pak()` changes nothing: download and install the new version. The navigation bar shows the version in use. See [Update](tutorials/01-installation.qmd#update).
:::

## Using the application

### Does Saíra send my data to the internet?

::: {.faq-card}
The spreadsheet does not leave the computer or the server where the app runs. These operations use the internet:

- **Name validation on GBIF** sends the scientific name. The IUCN category comes from the same query.
- **Background maps** ask the map provider for the images of the area that you see.
- **The Flora BR and Fauna BR update** looks for and downloads the new version from the JBRJ IPT. It sends none of your data.
- **`check_publication()`**, a function of the R package, queries the published dataset on GBIF or SiBBr.

The mapping, the Brazilian backbones and the coordinate tests work offline.
:::

### Which languages does the application work in?

::: {.faq-card}
Saíra is trilingual: **Portuguese (PT-BR)**, **English (EN-US)** and **Spanish (ES)**. You can switch the language at any time in the top corner of the interface. This help site is also available in all three languages (see the language buttons at the top).
:::

### Can I go back to a previous step without losing my work?

::: {.faq-card}
Yes. Going back to a step keeps the work: you can remap a field or validate again. Loading the spreadsheet again is different: a new file clears the validations, the generalization and the preview corrections.
:::

### Which spreadsheet formats does Saíra accept?

::: {.faq-card}
CSV (`.csv`, `.tsv`, `.txt`), with automatic encoding and separator detection, and Excel (`.xlsx`), read from the first sheet. It also accepts **camera-trap** packages (`.zip`): Camtrap DP and Wildlife Insights exports. Details in [Importing your data](tutorials/02-upload.qmd#if-the-file-reads-wrong).
:::

### Can I set a fixed value for the whole dataset?

::: {.faq-card}
Yes. These terms accept a **fixed value**: `rightsHolder`, `institutionCode`, `collectionCode`, `country`, `references`, `bibliographicCitation`, `geodeticDatum` and `basisOfRecord`. You type the value once on the card of the term and Saíra writes it to every row at export. See [Mapping fields to Darwin Core](tutorials/03-dwc-mapping.qmd).
:::

## Data and quality

### The accents in my spreadsheet show up broken. What should I do?

::: {.faq-card}
It is an encoding issue. Saíra detects the encoding by itself. If the accents are still wrong, save the spreadsheet as **CSV UTF-8** and upload it again. See [If the file reads wrong](tutorials/02-upload.qmd#if-the-file-reads-wrong).
:::

### Does Saíra automatically fix scientific names?

::: {.faq-card}
It **suggests** corrections from taxonomic backbones, but the final decision is always the specialist's. See [Validating scientific names](tutorials/05-name-validation.qmd).
:::

### How does Saíra handle threatened species?

::: {.faq-card}
In a dedicated **generalization** step, it flags threatened taxa (national MMA list) and helps you decide, species by species, whether and how much to reduce coordinate precision, following Chapman's (2020) decision table. See [Generalizing sensitive species](tutorials/07-generalization.qmd).
:::

### Does Saíra add the species' conservation status?

::: {.faq-card}
Yes. At export, it writes the status into the `dynamicProperties` field based on the backbones chosen in name validation: a Brazilian backbone (Flora BR or Fauna BR) adds the **MMA** category (`mmaThreatStatus`) and the source portaria (`mmaSource`); **GBIF** adds the global **IUCN** category (`iucnRedListCategory`). The MMA category comes from the national list. Saíra writes it to records from Brazil, by `country` or `countryCode`, and to records that it generalized. The IUCN category applies to any locality.
:::

## Export and publication

### What does Saíra produce in the end?

::: {.faq-card}
A **Darwin Core Archive (DwC-A)**: a `.zip` with `occurrence.txt`, `meta.xml`, `eml.xml` and, if there are measurements, `measurementorfact.txt`. The same `.zip` has the Excel copy, the mapping guide and, if there are corrections, `<dataset>-changes.csv`. The precise coordinates stay **outside** the `.zip`, in `<dataset>-sensitive-coords.xlsx`, which you download apart and do not publish. See [Package files](tutorials/08-export.qmd#package-files).
:::

### How do I publish the file on SiBBr or GBIF?

::: {.faq-card}
Publication happens outside Saíra, usually via your institution's or SiBBr's **IPT** (Integrated Publishing Toolkit). The generated file is already in the expected format.
:::

## Project

### What is Saíra's license?

::: {.faq-card}
Saíra is free software, licensed under the **GPL-3.0**. The code is available on [GitHub](https://github.com/rogerio-onza/saira).
:::

### I found a problem or have a suggestion. Where do I report it?

::: {.faq-card}
Open an *issue* on the [project repository on GitHub](https://github.com/rogerio-onza/saira).
:::
